h1: The 6 Best VEVOR Ultrasonic Cleaners of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best VEVOR Ultrasonic Cleaners: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 VEVOR ultrasonic cleaners from 1.3L to 30L, scored on tank size, transducer power, heater range and degassing controls.
summary: The VEVOR 6L with a 200W heater is the best all-rounder, matching a tank that fits tools and parts with 180W of ultrasonic power and a UL listing. The 15L steps up for engine parts and bigger batches. The 30L 600W model adds degas and gentle modes for shop work, and the 1.3L is the cheapest way to clean small items. Match tank size to your largest part, not your usual load.
intro: Ultrasonic cleaners fail buyers in a predictable way: they pick on tank volume and forget watts per liter. A big tank with weak transducers cleans slowly and unevenly, because cavitation bubbles thin out across the water. VEVOR sells everything from a 1.3L countertop unit to a 30L shop machine, so the lineup shows the tradeoff clearly.

We reviewed six VEVOR models from their published specs, comparing tank size, total ultrasonic watts, transducer count, heater range and special modes. Every unit here runs at 40kHz, which is the aggressive end of the range and suits tools, carburetors and hardware better than fragile jewelry. Ranking weights power density first, then heating, then controls.

products.name: VEVOR 6L 40kHz Ultrasonic Cleaner with Heater
products.verdict: The sweet spot of tank size, three transducers and a real heater for a home workshop.
products.description:
The 6L is built around a 304 stainless tank measuring 12.8 x 6.9 x 5.9 in, driven by 180W from three 60W transducers, with a 200W heater that reaches 80°C and a 0 to 30 minute timer. It is listed as FCC, CE, RoHS and UL.

That 30W per liter beats the 15L model's 24W and the 30L unit's 20W, so cavitation stays dense across the tank. It ranks above the 3L heated model because it adds three times the transducers for a modest size increase.

Buy it for tools, carburetor parts, eyewear and household hardware. The caveat is length: at 12.8 in, a long part will not fit flat.
cons: Tank too short for long parts
products.idealFor: Home workshops cleaning tools, small engine parts and hardware.
products.skipIf: You regularly clean parts longer than 12 in.

products.name: VEVOR 15L 40kHz Ultrasonic Cleaner, 360W with Heater
products.verdict: Six transducers and a 400W heater for engine parts and batch work.
products.description:
The 15L pairs six 60W transducers for 360W with a 400W heater running 0 to 80°C. The 304 stainless tank is 13 x 11.8 x 5.9 in, and the largest workpiece listed is 10.6 x 8.7 x 4.1 in.

Where the 6L suits tools, this model handles brake parts, carburetor bodies and a full tray of small items at once. It sits second because 24W per liter is lower than the 6L's 30W, so cleaning is slightly less intense, and it costs a tier more.

Choose it if you do batches or bigger components. The caveat is that the usable workpiece size is smaller than the tank, so measure parts against 10.6 x 8.7 in.
cons: Max workpiece is smaller than tank
products.idealFor: Auto hobbyists and small shops cleaning engine parts in batches.
products.skipIf: You only clean small household items.

products.name: VEVOR 30L Sonic Cleaner, 600W with Degas and Gentle Mode
products.verdict: Big 30L tank with 600W, degassing and a gentle setting for mixed shop loads.
products.description:
This 30L unit offers 600W of ultrasonic power at 40kHz, heating from 0 to 80°C and two special modes: degassing and gentle, which is a lower power setting. The tank is 304 stainless steel.

Degassing matters because dissolved air in fresh water dampens cavitation, so running it first speeds up the first cycle. It ranks above the knob-controlled 30L because the listing gives a clear wattage, and 600W across 30L is 20W per liter. That is lower density than the 6L.

It is built for racks of parts and larger items. The caveat is footprint and cost: it needs a dedicated bench and a lot of cleaning solution to fill.
products.idealFor: Shops cleaning racks of parts or oversized items.
products.skipIf: A countertop footprint is all you have room for.

products.name: VEVOR 3L Heated Ultrasonic Cleaner with Digital Timer
products.verdict: A countertop heater and dual fuse protection in a 3L tank.
products.description:
The 3L holds 0.8 gal in a 304 stainless tank, with two 60W transducers for 120W, heating from room temperature to 80°C and a 0 to 30 minute timer. Dual fuse protection and anti-slip feet are listed.

It delivers 40W per liter, the highest density in this group, which makes small parts clean fast. It ranks behind the 6L because the tank is smaller, so wrenches and carburetors will not fit, and it ranks above the plain 1.3L because it adds a heater.

It suits glasses, jewelry that tolerates 40kHz, watch bands and small tools. The caveat is capacity: anything over a few inches deep needs a larger tank.
products.idealFor: Small tools, eyewear and watch parts on a countertop.
products.skipIf: Your parts are longer than the 3L tank.

products.name: VEVOR 30L Ultrasonic Cleaner with Knob Control
products.verdict: Knob control for time, temperature and frequency, plus basket and cleaning ball.
products.description:
This 30L stainless tank runs at 40kHz with degassing mode and dual power settings, and the control knobs set frequency, time and temperature. A basket and cleaning ball come in the box.

Knobs are easier to operate with gloved hands than a digital panel, which is its niche. It ranks below the 600W model because the listing gives no total wattage, so you cannot judge power density. It also trails the 6L on proof of power and certification.

Buy it for a shop where gloves and grease are routine. The caveat is the missing wattage: ask the seller before committing, since a 30L tank with low power cleans unevenly.
products.idealFor: Greasy shop environments where knob controls win.
products.skipIf: You want confirmed wattage and a certification listing.

products.name: VEVOR 1.3L 40kHz Ultrasonic Cleaner, Digital Timer
products.verdict: The cheapest way into VEVOR ultrasonics, with a single 60W transducer and no heater.
products.description:
The 1.3L has a 6.1 x 5.5 x 2.6 in stainless tank, one 60W transducer at 40kHz and a 0 to 30 minute digital timer. It plugs into a 110V outlet, and the listing says heating is not offered.

It delivers about 46W per liter, strong density, but with a 2.6 in tank depth only flat items fit. It ranks last because the 3L adds a heater for a small step up in price, and heat is the biggest lift in cleaning performance with detergent.

It works for rings, dentures, razor heads and eyeglass frames. The caveat is depth: tall items will not submerge.
products.idealFor: Rings, eyewear and small flat items on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You want to clean with heated solution.

methodology.title: Power density
methodology.description: We divide total ultrasonic watts by tank volume, because dense cavitation cleans faster than a big tank with weak output.

methodology.title: Tank size and fit
methodology.description: Tank dimensions and maximum workpiece size decide which parts you can actually clean.

methodology.title: Heating
methodology.description: Heater wattage and range matter because warm solution loosens grease and residue.

methodology.title: Special modes
methodology.description: Degassing and gentle settings extend what each unit can handle.

methodology.title: Safety and certification
methodology.description: Fuse protection and listed certifications give confidence in a mains-powered tank of water.

whatMatters.detail: Total ultrasonic watts divided by liters tells you how dense the cavitation is. A 6L tank at 180W gives 30W per liter, while a 30L tank at 600W gives 20. Divide the listed wattage by the tank volume before comparing models, and favor density over raw capacity for stubborn grease.

Warm solution cleans oils and flux far better than cold, because heat thins grease and speeds the chemistry. Look for a heater range such as 0 to 80°C and a wattage like 200W or 400W. A unit with no heater cleans, but expect longer cycles and weaker results on grease.

The tank is the outer limit, but the usable workpiece size is smaller. The 15L lists 10.6 x 8.7 x 4.1 in of usable space inside a 13 x 11.8 in tank. Measure your longest part, then compare it to the stated workpiece size rather than the tank.

Fresh tap water holds dissolved air, which absorbs ultrasound and weakens cavitation. A degas cycle runs the transducers briefly to drive the air out before cleaning. If you refill often or use deep tanks like the 30L models, a degas mode saves several minutes per batch.

A mains-powered water tank is a shock hazard if it fails. A listing that names FCC, CE, RoHS and UL, as the 6L does, or dual fuse protection, as the 3L does, shows the maker thought about safety. Scan the listing for those words before buying.

faq.q: Will these VEVOR cleaners work on jewelry?
faq.a: All run at 40kHz, which is aggressive. Hard metals like gold and steel tolerate it, but soft stones and pearls do not. The 30L gentle mode helps, though for fragile pieces a unit above 40kHz is the safer choice.

faq.q: What is the common mistake buyers make?
faq.a: Buying by tank volume alone. A 30L tank at 600W gives only 20W per liter, below the 6L's 30W. Check total watts and transducer count, like the 15L's six 60W units, before you trust the size.

faq.q: Is the 15L worth it over the 6L?
faq.a: Only if your parts exceed 12 in or you clean batches. The 15L has 360W and a 400W heater, but 24W per liter is lower than the 6L. For tools and small parts, the 6L cleans more intensely.

faq.q: How do I set one up for the first run?
faq.a: Fill with water and detergent to the line, run the degas mode if the unit has one, and warm the heater toward 80°C. The 3L and 6L list timers up to 30 minutes, so start short and repeat.

faq.q: How do I maintain the stainless tank?
faq.a: Drain after each session, wipe the 304 stainless tank dry and clean any residue ring. Avoid running the transducers empty, since all these units rely on liquid to carry the energy, and never run the heater dry.

faq.q: Can I clean parts directly on the tank bottom?
faq.a: No. Parts should sit in the included basket on the 30L models, or in a beaker on smaller units like the 1.3L. Direct contact with the bottom can dampen the transducers and may scratch the tank.

finalTake: The VEVOR 6L with heater is the right buy for most people, because its 30W per liter and UL listing beat much larger tanks. Step up to the 15L only for big batches, and to the 30L 600W model for shop racks. Drop to the 1.3L only for light, flat items, and always measure your longest part first.
